items.title: Show HN: DepWarden – free, anonymous dependency vulnerability scanner
items.contentSnippet:
No account, no source upload — paste a manifest/lockfile and get OSV+KEV+EPSS-prioritized findings in a session-isolated workspace. Also ran a typosquat study: checked every single-char typo of the 30 most popular npm/PyPI packages against the real registries and OSV's malicious-package DB — 32.7% of registered npm look-alikes are already confirmed malicious. Data/methodology:https://depwarden.in/blog/npm-pypi-typosquatting-2026-report

items.title: Digital Fluency Is the Missing Foundation in K-12 Career Pathways
items.contentSnippet:
What separates a student who can use a digital tool from one who can build something new with it? Kimberly Smith of Digital Promise argues that digital fluency, not just digital literacy, is the foundational skill K-12 career pathways have been missing. Drawing on credentialed cybersecurity programs in rural Alabama and a six-part fluency framework, this piece offers a clear, actionable case for why every career pathway, in every industry, must embed digital fluency now.

items.title: Show HN: Crew — Let Claude/Codex/OpenCode agents talk to each other
items.contentSnippet:
crew hooks into your favorite CLI agent and injects a brief context of every other running agent (status, goal, recap, last few transcript entries). It also gives agents an interface to message each other, landing messages in another agent's context even mid-work.
Since starting to use crew I've discovered plenty of use cases: 
- shipping on a single checkout without worktrees
- cross-agent code review
- Fable supervisor overseeing GPT-5.6 execution

items.contentSnippet:

This addresses both the consumer problem with passive feeds and the creator problem of interactive work being flattened into videos, images, or links.
